subject: Fleet patterns & data-sovereignty tradeoffs for CareCentric regulated rollout
messages:
From: CareCentric IT <itops@carecentric.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@carecentric.com, alex@cloudoptics.io
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity guidance needed for regulated pilot (PHI scope)

Hi Jonas,

We're moving forward with a pilot that will process PHI and must be isolated to US-only infrastructure with audit logging and KMS in our tenancy. We have a rough usage profile: ~250 peak concurrent sessions, average prompt+response 900 tokens, expected 18M tokens/month in steady state for phase 1. The security team is insisting on either Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or Private (VPC with a customer-managed control plane).

Can you help sketch the performance/econ tradeoffs and an initial sizing footprint for both paths? Procurement will need this to evaluate committed vs burst pricing. Also include brief notes on canary rollout strategy (we want low blast radius).

Thanks,
Sam Lee
Senior IT Ops, CareCentric

[Attachment: carecentric_requirements.pdf (stub)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sam Lee <itops@carecentric.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity guidance needed for regulated pilot (PHI scope)

Sam — thanks for the clear profile. I've put together an initial matrix (attached) and a high-level recommendation below. Quick summary: Dedicated reserved capacity gives better unit economics and predictable latency for high sustained volume; Private gives the strongest control for compliance, slightly higher cost, and more operational overhead.

Highlights (short):
- Baseline demand: 250 concurrent sessions -> target steady-state concurrency headroom 320 (20% buffer).
- Recommended Dedicated slate: 12x A100-80GB instances (reserved), autoscale pool to 20 for burst windows. This supports continuous batching, gives predictable 95th pct latency ~150-220ms token latency depending on prompt shape.
- Recommended Private slate: 6x H100-80GB nodes with single-tenant VPC + KMS integration in customer tenancy. Because Private avoids noisy neighbors and can use larger model variants, we recommend 6 nodes with higher per-node utilization but plan for a +50% buffer for guidance -> operationally similar to 9 nodes for safety.
- Cost tradeoff: Dedicated reserved (12 + burst) is ~15-25% cheaper per token at scale vs Private baseline, assuming 12–18 month commitment. Private has added support/ops and audit costs.

Canary proposal (attached timeline):
1) Week 0–2: Deploy Private control plane in US region + dev testing with synthetic PHI PII masked set.
2) Week 3–4: Canary to 5% traffic on dedicated pool (small model quantized) with KV prefix cache warmed.
3) Week 5–6: Expand to 30% if no perf/quality regression.

I attached carecentric_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx — it has expected RPS->GPU mapping, token/sec estimates, and cost sensitivity to batching and quantization.

If helpful, I can run a short perf sweep with your sample prompt set to verify latencies; Alex from CloudOptics, can you help coordinate?

— Jonas Weber
Director, Deal Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-22T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Capacity guidance needed for regulated pilot (PHI scope)

Notes on procurement path:
- Procurement will prefer a delta view: incremental monthly committed cost vs burst cost at expected 18M tokens/month. I'll draft two line items: (A) Dedicated committed 12 nodes (12-month) and (B) Private single-tenant support + infra runrate.
- For SLA/credits ask: recommend offering a 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated; for Private, offer operational playbooks and 48h incident lead.
- Also flag that model quantization (8-bit/4-bit where safe) materially reduces GPU counts; include a conservative quality delta bucket.

Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sam Lee <itops@carecentric.com>, procurement@carecentric.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, alex@cloudoptics.io
Date: 2027-06-23T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: Dedicated vs Private sizing + operational notes (CareCentric)

Hi Sam / Procurement team —

Attached is a compact proposal that compares two implementation lanes for your PHI-scoped pilot. Key callouts below:

Dedicated lane (recommended if committed throughput > ~12M tokens/mo):
- Config: 12x A100-80GB reserved + autoscale to 20
- Throughput: supports ~300 concurrent sessions with steady TTL caching + dynamic batching; expected 18M tokens/mo comfortably handled at 70–80% utilization
- Ops: Redwood-managed control plane, per-request logging, tenant isolation at network/instance level, KMS integration (Redwood-hosted keys or customer-managed KMS for enterprise tier)
- Pros: best unit cost, simpler procurement, faster onboarding (~2–3 weeks)
- Cons: less surface control for audit ingestion into customer SIEM without private tenancy integration

Private lane (recommended if customer-managed KMS and full control of audit streams is mandatory):
- Config: 6x H100-80GB initially; recommend planning budget for expansion to 9 nodes to account for maintenance windows and perf variance
- Throughput: similar tail latency advantages for single-tenant workloads; higher per-node utilization but narrower scaling envelope
- Ops: customer VPC + private control plane, direct KMS/HSM integration, full audit log export to your SIEM, customer-managed backups of model artifacts
- Pros: strongest compliance posture, data sovereignty control
- Cons: higher TCO and longer lead time (~4–6 weeks), Redwood-run ops add-on recommended

Attachments included: capacity matrix + canary_rollout_timeline.pdf with step-by-step gating criteria (quality gates, perf SLOs, fallback rules).

Next steps: Please confirm which lane Procurement prefers so we can finalize pricing (committed tokens vs burst) and produce SOW language. Happy to jump on a call this week to walk through the matrix.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: carecentric_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx]

From: procurement@carecentric.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, itops@carecentric.com, alex@cloudoptics.io
Date: 2027-06-24T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated vs Private sizing + operational notes (CareCentric)

Thanks Marissa — couple of clarifying items before we move to SOW:
1) For the Private lane: will the KMS/HSM integration require additional on-prem hardware, or can we leverage our cloud KMS in our account? Any limitations on key rotation frequency?
2) If we choose Dedicated with a 12-node reserved slate, what is the defined burst-to-bill behavior when autoscale goes to 20? We need clear caps for monthly spend forecasting.
3) Can you confirm the expected 95th percentile token latency difference between the two lanes for our sample prompt set?

Also, please provide a single-page procurement-ready summary with line items (reserved nodes, burst allowance, support add-on, onboarding fee).

— Priya N.
Sr. Procurement Specialist, CareCentric

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Priya N. <procurement@carecentric.com>, Sam Lee <itops@carecentric.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, alex@cloudoptics.io
Date: 2027-06-24T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: Dedicated vs Private sizing + operational notes (CareCentric)

Priya — thanks, quick answers inline and offering next-step deliverables below.

1) KMS/HSM for Private lane:
- You can use your cloud KMS in your account (recommended). Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) with rotation policies you control; rotation frequency is customer-configurable — we recommend 90-day rotation as a conservative default. If you require FIPS-level HSM appliances on-prem, that is possible but adds procurement lead time.

2) Burst-to-bill behavior for Dedicated:
- Billing model we propose in the procurement summary: baseline charge = committed 12-node monthly fee (flat). Burst usage up to 20 nodes is billed at a capped hourly premium rate; we will provide a monthly burst cap option (e.g., max 200 burst-hours/month at premium rate) to give a spending ceiling. We'll include both a conservative and high-usage cap in the summary.

3) 95th percentile token latency (sample prompts):
- Dedicated (12x A100, quantized medium model): ~180–240ms/token 95th pct
- Private (6x H100, full precision variant): ~140–200ms/token 95th pct
- Note: these numbers depend heavily on batching policy and prefix/KV cache hit rate — we note a 20–35% tail improvement if prefix caching can be warmed by user session keys.

Deliverables in 24–48h: procurement-ready one-pager (line items + burst cap scenarios), updated XLS with cost bins for quantization choices, and a short canary run checklist. We can also schedule a 30-min review with Alex to confirm perf baselines with your prompt set.

If that all sounds right, I'll send the one-pager and revised attachments by tomorrow EOD.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Deal Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary_rollout_timeline.pdf]
